findings.element: Settings configurator overlay (opened from 'Set up matching')
findings.finding: The page behind the overlay is not made inert while the overlay is open, so the overlay does not actually trap focus.
findings.user_impact: A keyboard user tabbing through the overlay can tab straight past its last control onto background page elements, losing the modal context and potentially acting on controls they can no longer see.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the background inert (e.g. inert attribute or aria-hidden plus a focus trap) for as long as the overlay is open, per the standard dialog pattern.

evidence.action: opened the configurator and checked background reachability while it was open
evidence.observed: environment record: page behind the overlay inert while open = false

findings.finding: Pressing Escape while the overlay is open does not close it.
findings.user_impact: A keyboard-only or screen-reader user relying on the standard Escape-to-dismiss convention has no way to close the overlay except by tabbing to and activating the small × Close control.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind the Escape key to the same close/discard handler as the × Close button.

evidence.action: pressed Escape with the overlay open (focus at open was on the 'openRules' control)

findings.element: Narrow the search — checkbox with no accessible name
findings.finding: The checkbox that scopes/narrows the invoice search exposes no accessible name.
findings.user_impact: A screen-reader user hears only 'checkbox, checked/unchecked' with no indication of what condition it toggles, so they can't tell what turning it on or off does.
findings.suggested_fix: Associate a visible <label> (or aria-label) with the checkbox stating the condition it controls.

evidence.action: inspected accessible name while toggling checked state false → true → true
evidence.observed: accessible name recorded as '(no accessible name) input'

findings.element: Narrow the search — select with no accessible name
findings.finding: The select that chooses which field to match on (invoice number / payment note) exposes no accessible name.
findings.user_impact: A screen-reader user hears only the current combo-box value with no label for what it belongs to, so they can't tell what choice they're making without sight of the surrounding text.
findings.suggested_fix: Attach a visible label or aria-label describing the field, e.g. 'Match on field'.

evidence.action: inspected accessible name while changing value invoice_number → payment_note → invoice_number
evidence.observed: accessible name recorded as '(no accessible name) select'

gaps: Focus visibility: the state map records checked/value transitions and reachability for every control but never confirms a visible focus indicator on any of them; whether focus is visibly shown at each step is unverified, not assumed to pass.

Focus return on close: neither the Close (×) pass nor the Escape pass records where focus lands after the overlay closes, so whether focus returns to the 'Configure / Set up matching' trigger is unknown.

Tab order: the map gives a per-zone control inventory and confirms each control is independently reachable, but records no key-by-key Tab traversal, so whether focus moves in the order the screen reads (including into/out of the 'then refine' repeating group) is unconfirmed.

'×' remove-condition button: accessible name is recorded only as '×' with no data on how it's disambiguated when more than one condition row exists; not enough evidence to call this a finding, but it is untested.
